title: Worldview Data Extraction Pipeline
description: Create a pipeline to extract structured worldview settings (term, nature, detail, source) from novel chapters. Inspired by BookWorld's term-based extraction method. Enables setting-aware agent prompts and worldview coherence validation.
action: Create src-ts/narrative/worldview-extractor.ts with extractWorldview(chapters) function implementing: chunk text → extract atomic facts via LLM → filter character actions + common sense → cluster similar entries → produce WorldviewSetting[] with term/nature/detail/source fields. Add src-ts/mcp/endpoints/m11-worldview.ts endpoint for extraction trigger and retrieval. Register in container/bindings.ts. Export from narrative/index.ts.

convergence.verification: Import { extractWorldview, WorldviewSetting } from narrative/worldview-extractor. Call with mock chapter content, verify it returns WorldviewSetting[] with required fields.
convergence.definition_of_done: Worldview extraction pipeline exists as a standalone module that accepts chapter content and produces structured worldview settings. MCP endpoint exposes extraction and retrieval.

files.change: New file: WorldviewSetting interface {term, nature, detail, source}, extractWorldview(chapters, llmService) function with chunk→extract→filter→cluster pipeline
New file: POST /worldview/extract (trigger extraction for project), GET /worldview/{projectId} (retrieve extracted worldview settings)

implementation: Create src-ts/narrative/worldview-extractor.ts: define WorldviewSetting interface with term: string, nature: string (artifact|social_norm|custom|geography|magic_system|political), detail: string, source: string (chapter ref). Define WorldviewExtractor class with async extract(chapters: ChapterContent[]): Promise<WorldviewSetting[]> implementing 4-step pipeline: 1) split chapters into ~500-word chunks, 2) call LLM to extract worldview facts as {term, nature, detail}, 3) filter out character actions and common-sense items, 4) cluster similar entries by term similarity, merge details

Create src-ts/mcp/endpoints/m11-worldview.ts following pattern from m10-style.ts: define route handlers for POST /worldview/extract (accepts projectId, triggers extraction, returns settings count) and GET /worldview/{projectId} (returns cached settings). Use existing request/response types from gateway-route-types.ts
Update src-ts/mcp/endpoints/index.ts to export { registerWorldviewEndpoints } from m11-worldview.ts
Update src-ts/narrative/index.ts to add export { WorldviewSetting, WorldviewExtractor } from './worldview-extractor'
Update src-ts/container/bindings.ts to bind WorldviewExtractor to its interface, inject LLM service dependency
Verify: cd src-ts && npx tsc --noEmit passes

unit: WorldviewExtractor: extract from single chapter produces WorldviewSetting[] with required fields
WorldviewExtractor: filter removes character action sentences
WorldviewExtractor: cluster merges entries with similar terms
WorldviewExtractor: empty input returns empty array

reference.pattern: BookWorld worldview extraction: chunk → atomic facts → filter → cluster → terminology (term/nature/detail/source)
reference.examples: m10-style.ts shows pattern for MCP endpoints that trigger LLM-powered extraction and cache results

rationale.chosen_approach: Standalone module with its own class rather than extending knowledge-service
decision_factors: Domain-specific extraction logic (narrative worldview) differs from general knowledge CRUD
BookWorld's validated extraction pipeline provides proven methodology
Separation enables independent testing and iteration
rationale.tradeoffs: Extra module vs extending knowledge-service, but cleaner separation of concerns

risks: LLM extraction quality varies by model — cache results and allow manual edit
